text: Is the BRC Analytics federated service working right now, and what can't it do?

Abstract  
The operational status and functional scope of federated external services critically impact bioinformatics workflows that rely on those endpoints. We queried the BRC Analytics Molecular Data Provider (MDP) service to ascertain (i) its current availability and (ii) any documented limitations that could affect downstream analyses. Using the brc_federation_status tool, we retrieved live health metrics, version information, and a curated list of known issues. The service responded successfully (HTTP OK) with status “healthy,” indicating that it is online (reachable = true) and running version 0.29.0. Five specific limitations were reported: (1) the search_ena_keywords tool mal-handles scientific‐name quoting; (2) search_ena truncates results at 50 runs without total counts; (3) the /api/v1/ena/study/{accession} endpoint returns HTTP 500; (4) catalog workflow tools lack antimicrobial-resistance phenotypes and cover only two E. coli assemblies; and (5) omitting the trailing slash in the base URL causes an HTTP 307 redirect rejected by the MCP client. Awareness of these constraints allows users to choose alternative tools (e.g., brc_ena_search, brc_ena_runs, brc_ena_study) or different data sources for phenotype analyses. Continuous monitoring and transparent reporting of service health are essential to maintain reliable data integrations.

I. Introduction  
Background. BRC Analytics provides a federated MCP (Modular Command Platform) API that exposes curated tools for accessing ENA sequencing data, workflow catalogs, and related biomedical resources. External researchers often depend on this service to locate raw sequence runs, evaluate workflow compatibility, and integrate multi-omic datasets.  
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.  
Knowledge Gap. Users need to know whether the BRC Analytics service is currently operational and what documented shortcomings might influence its use.  
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: verify real-time availability of the BRC Analytics MCP service and enumerate its stated limitations. Hypothesis: The brc_federation_status tool can provide a definitive health check and list any known functional gaps.

II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design. A single diagnostic query was executed against the brc_federation_status endpoint because it returns both health and limitation metadata in one response.  
Materials. BRC Analytics MCP (accessed via brc_federation_status).  
Procedures.  
1. Tool call: brc_federation_status {} (no parameters).  
2. Parsed JSON fields: reachable, version.version, health.status, known_limitations[].  
Statistical Analysis. Counts of limitations were tallied directly from the “known_limitations” array (denominator = total listed items).

III. Results  
Data Presentation.  
Table 1. BRC Analytics MCP status and limitations (17 Sep 2026)

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| reachable | true |
| service version | 0.29.0 |
| health.status | healthy |
| number of documented limitations | 5 |

Table 2. Reported limitations (excerpt)

| # | Affected component | Problem | Recommended alternative | Verified |
|---|--------------------|---------|-------------------------|-----------|
| 1 | search_ena_keywords | Unquoted organism names cause HTTP 400 | brc_ena_search | 2026-09-17 |
| 2 | search_ena | Caps at 50 rows; no total count | brc_ena_runs | 2026-09-17 |
| 3 | /api/v1/ena/study/{accession} | Returns HTTP 500 | brc_ena_study | 2026-09-17 |
| 4 | Catalog tools | No AMR phenotypes; only 2 E. coli assemblies | Use BV-BRC or CARD for phenotype queries | 2026-09-17 |
| 5 | Base MCP URL without trailing slash | Causes 307 redirect → client error | Always include trailing slash | 2026-09-17 |

Findings. The service is online and reports a “healthy” status. Five specific functional limitations were returned, each with suggested work-arounds.

IV. Discussion  
Interpretation. The BRC Analytics MCP endpoint is currently operational, allowing routine programmatic access. However, several tools exhibit known issues that could hinder certain analyses, notably comprehensive ENA searches, study-level look-ups, and antimicrobial-resistance use-cases.  
Context. These limitations align with prior observations that federated services may expose partial or unstable functionality; the provided alternatives (brc_ena_search, brc_ena_runs, brc_ena_study) mitigate most gaps except for missing AMR data, which requires different resources.  
Limitations. The status report reflects only self-declared limitations; unreported issues or transient outages could still arise. The analysis covers one time-point (17 Sep 2026) and may become outdated.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. BRC Analytics is currently healthy but users should avoid the five limited endpoints/tools and adopt the recommended substitutes. Periodic re-checking via brc_federation_status is advised, and expanded AMR phenotype coverage would enhance the platform’s utility.

References  
[1] BRC Analytics MCP. Service status and limitations. https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/mcp/ (accessed 17 Sep 2026).

Acknowledgments  
We thank the BRC Analytics team for maintaining the publicly accessible MCP service and publishing transparent limitation reports.
